title: DurableJobV1
description: One durable background job as a service records it (document 13 section 6.4). Carries the command binding, the externally visible state, the lease a worker holds, cancellation intent, the waiting reason when progress is blocked, and the terminal result. A reader validates a stored row against this before believing any field in it.
$comment: WHY THIS DOCUMENT EXISTS. `FND-003` task 2 owes 'durable job states/attempts/leases/cancellation/terminal result', and `schemas/jobs/` held only a `.gitkeep` since 2026-07-30 -- the directory was not even in `FOUNDATION_SCHEMA_DIRS`, so anything dropped into it resolved to nothing. Meanwhile `evidence_review_service` shipped the whole subsystem (`ER-M020`/`FND-006`, migration 0020) and runs it in production against no released grammar at all, which is the same defect the event-envelope release repaired. AUTHORING DECISION 1 - THIS DOCUMENT IS FLAT, AND DELIBERATELY. The obvious tidier shape groups lease, cancellation and waiting into sub-objects. It was rejected: the justification for releasing this grammar now is that a second service must be able to implement the SAME subsystem, and the only unambiguous description of `durable_jobs` is its own column set. A nested regrouping would be a design invented here, and every consumer would have to translate. Member names are the live column names. AUTHORING DECISION 2 - `state` IS THE SIX-VALUE EXTERNAL ENUM, AND `cancel_requested` IS NOT IN IT. Section 13.6.4 is explicit that cancellation intent is a timestamped flag while external status remains `queued`, `running` or `waiting`; a seventh state would make every consumer's switch wrong. The intent is carried by `cancel_requested_at`/`cancel_requested_by`, both-or-neither. AUTHORING DECISION 3 - TERMINALITY IS EXPRESSED AS A CROSS-FIELD RULE, NOT A COMMENT. `terminal_at` is required exactly when `state` is terminal, and `error_code` exactly when `state` is `failed`. Document 13 says 'terminal state is immutable'; a grammar that admits a terminal row with no terminal instant cannot detect the row that broke it. AUTHORING DECISION 4 - THE LEASE HAS NO FENCE TOKEN, BECAUSE THE IMPLEMENTATION HAS NONE. `worker_id` + `lease_expires_at` + `heartbeat_at` is the whole mechanism: a running row is never a claim candidate, so a lease is not stealable and expiry is repaired by a reaper that seals the attempt as `lease_expired`. Adding a fence field here would describe a system that does not exist. AUTHORING DECISION 5 - PAYLOAD-MINIMAL IS ENFORCED, NOT REQUESTED. Section 13.6.4 says large inputs and outputs are immutable artifact refs and progress carries bounded structured facts. So `progress` and `result_summary` are objects, `error_detail` is capped at 512 characters to match the live CHECK, and there is no member anywhere in this document that can hold licensed text, an extracted value or a credential. THIS DOCUMENT IS DELIBERATELY NOT a queue protocol. It does not describe how a worker claims, how long a lease may be, what the retry policy is, or what a job type means. Those are configuration and per-service policy; section 13.6.4 leaves them open on purpose and pinning them here would freeze one service's tuning into a fleet contract.

schema_ref.$comment: A const, the envelope idiom. A reader holding a stored row has to know which grammar it is reading before it can check anything in it.

job_id.$comment: This job's own identity. Section 09 says IDs are opaque UUIDs; a retry is a new attempt under this same id, never a second job.

tenant_id.$comment: The owning tenant. Required and never null: section 13.6.2 forbids binding a global operation to an empty tenant value, so a job with no tenant is not expressible rather than silently global.

job_type.$comment: Which registered command this job runs. A canonical type token, so the value space is the fleet's and not one service's spelling.

state.$comment: The externally visible state. See authoring decision 2 -- `cancel_requested` is deliberately absent.

command_hash.$comment: Binds the job to its exact command. Section 13.3.2 requires RFC 8785 canonicalisation for command, idempotency and input-snapshot hashes; a service that invents a local JSON sorting recipe produces a hash no other service can reproduce.

input_snapshot_hash.$comment: The inputs as they stood when the job was enqueued, where the command reads any. Same canonicalisation as `command_hash`.

idempotency_key.$comment: The caller's key, when one was supplied. Uniqueness is scoped per service and is not expressible in a document grammar; this member only says the key was recorded.

profile_version.$comment: The profile pinned at enqueue time, so a later profile change cannot retroactively reinterpret a finished run.

capability_version.$comment: The capability version the worker claimed under. Section 13.6.4 records it at claim time precisely so an attempt can be read back against the code that ran it.

pack_refs.$comment: References to the packs in force. References, never pack contents -- section 13.6.1 keeps operational rows to IDs, hashes and authorized refs.

correlation_id.$comment: The correlation this job belongs to. Excluded from `command_hash` by section 13.3.2, because a retry under a new correlation is the same command.

causation_id.$comment: What caused this job. Same exclusion from the hash as `correlation_id`.

workflow_ref.$comment: The workflow step that enqueued this, where one did.

originating_subject_id.$comment: WHO asked, as a reference. Section 09 derives actor and tenant from authentication and never accepts them as authoritative body fields; this records the derived subject and carries no credential.

originating_actor_role.$comment: The role that subject held. A reference to a role name, not an entitlement grant.

attempt.$comment: How many attempts have been started. Zero for a job that has never been claimed; monotonic thereafter.

max_attempts.$comment: The attempt ceiling from the retry policy. At least one: a job that may never be attempted is not a job.

worker_id.$comment: The lease holder. Present exactly while a lease is held; the reaper clears it when a lease expires. See authoring decision 4.

lease_expires_at.$comment: When this lease stops being valid. Bounded by service configuration, which this document deliberately does not pin.

heartbeat_at.$comment: The last heartbeat from the holder. A heartbeat extends the lease; it does not re-grant it.

cancel_requested_at.$comment: When cancellation was requested. Intent cannot be withdrawn, so this member only ever appears.

cancel_requested_by.$comment: Who requested cancellation, as a subject reference. Both-or-neither with `cancel_requested_at`: a request with no requester is not attributable and is refused here rather than stored.

waiting_reason.$comment: The typed reason a job cannot progress. Section 13.6.4 requires it on entering `waiting`, and requires that entering `waiting` never retains a human credential -- so this is a token, not a message.

waiting_dependency_ref.$comment: The dependency or provider attempt being waited on, as a reference.

reconcile_after.$comment: When a reconciler should look again. An instant, not a duration: a duration is only meaningful relative to a write time the reader may not have.

callback_state.$comment: How the callback to the originating system stands. Section 13.10.2 is emphatic that callback delivery is never proof of application, so this is a delivery fact and never a domain outcome.

progress.$comment: Bounded structured facts only. See authoring decision 5 -- never full licensed text, never an unbounded array.

result_summary.$comment: The terminal result as bounded facts. Anything large is a ref in `result_artifact_ref`, never inlined here.

result_artifact_ref.$comment: The immutable artifact holding the real output. A ref, never an expiring URL -- section 13.3.2 is explicit.

run_manifest_ref.$comment: The run manifest for this execution, where the job type produces one.

error_code.$comment: The typed failure. Required exactly when `state` is `failed` -- see authoring decision 3 -- so a failed job can never be untriageable.

error_detail.$comment: A bounded diagnostic. Capped at 512 characters to match the live constraint, because an uncapped detail field is where licensed text leaks into an operational table.

queued_at.$comment: When the job entered the queue. Always present: every job was queued, including one already terminal.

started_at.$comment: When the first attempt started. Absent for a job never claimed.

terminal_at.$comment: When the job reached a terminal state. Required exactly when `state` is terminal; see authoring decision 3.

allOf.$comment: Terminality, in the grammar. A terminal state without the instant it became terminal is the row that proves the writer skipped the transition guard.
A failed job names its failure. Section 13.6.4 gives `error_code` as the typed outcome; without this rule `failed` with no code validates and nothing downstream can route it.
Waiting declares why and when to look again -- both, per section 13.6.4. A `waiting` row missing either is a job nothing will ever reconcile.

sealed.$comment: The closed form, for a consumer that composes this document into a larger one and still wants unknown members refused.
